clue.text: This, worn under a skirt, is a good way to start affair with porter

indicators.note: says the first piece comes at the start of the answer

parts.note: a good way off means far
an affair or matter is a thing
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A tip on beginning a romance with a hotel porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This, worn under a skirt' is the definition: the clue points at itself. 'to start' puts FAR first, then THING and ALE follow; 'is' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A farthingale was a hooped frame of whalebone worn beneath Tudor and Elizabethan skirts to spread them out.

clue.text: Upfront guy and girl protecting old remains

indicators.note: the girl's name wraps around and shields the other two pieces

parts.note: Fay is a girl's name
the remains are the rest

explanation.surface: A frank man and a girl look after some ancient relics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is a rope here, not a man: a forward rope. 'protecting' puts O and REST inside FAY.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship a forestay is the rope running from the masthead down to the bow, a guy at the front.

clue.text: Poet has Italian girl introduced to hill climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the assembled letters upward, from the bottom
the girl's name is put inside the hill word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
Tess is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A poet keeps an Italian girl who has been brought along on a hill walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' puts TESS inside TOR, giving TTESSOR; with I in front that is ITTESSOR, and 'climbing' reads it upward. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti and his sister Christina were Victorian poets.

clue.text: Old king's staff overseen by His Excellency

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
a staff is a rod

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch's employees are supervised by an ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a stick, ROD. The 's of 'king's' means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod the Great was the king of Judea in the Gospel nativity story.

clue.text: Rise in metal cost is radical

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: tin is a metal
a cost or charge is a rate

explanation.surface: A jump in metal prices is drastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' reads as an adjective (extreme) but is the chemist's noun: a group of atoms acting as a unit. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms that behaves as one unit, and the NO3 group is a classic example.

clue.text: Old city supports a match that's played just for pleasure

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the others

parts.note: to match is to mate or pair up
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city backs a contest that is held only for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts UR below A and MATE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for love of the game rather than for pay, so an amateur sport is one done for enjoyment.

clue.text: Real idiot upset leader

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A true fool has knocked over the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a boss, but in newspapers a leader is the main opinion article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers the leader is the editor's opinion column, also called the leading article.

clue.text: A certain set of changes to hairstyle

explanation.surface: A particular series of alterations to someone's haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' is a bell-ringing term: a change is one order in which a set of bells is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: In change-ringing a bob is a particular call altering the sequence (as in Plain Bob); a bob is also a short haircut level with the jaw.

clue.text: Fortification for French island in cove

indicators.note: the French word sits within the word for a cove

parts.note: a cove is a small bay
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: A fort for a French island stands in a sheltered inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailey is the walled courtyard of a castle, part of its defensive works.

clue.text: Boxer keeping hat under bar

indicators.note: in a down clue the hat piece is placed beneath the other

parts.note: to bar is to ban
a tam is a Scottish woolly hat, short for tam-o'-shanter

explanation.surface: A fighter wears his hat while standing at the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub counter but is the verb, BAN. 'keeping' is a link word. Boxing weight classes include bantamweight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a boxer in the bantamweight class, a light division.

clue.text: Endlessly endanger queen in flight

indicators.note: says the word for endanger loses its last letter

parts.note: to endanger is to risk
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: Putting a queen in endless danger while she flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the K from RISK. 'in flight' looks like fleeing but means in a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical part of a step, one of many in a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Usual practice of antiriot assembly capturing dissident leader

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the extra letter inside them
the letters of the word are assembled into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A habit of riot-control squads is seizing the head of a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges ANTIRIOT, and 'capturing' puts D, the first letter of 'dissident', inside it. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom handed down, the customary way things are done.

clue.text: Bird kept by regiment in the end

indicators.note: the kept and regiment pieces go inside the word for end

parts.note: an end or purpose is a sake, as in 'for the sake of'
kept means held
R is a standard abbreviation for regiment, as in military unit titles

explanation.surface: A bird held captive by the army until the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' is a purpose here, SAKE ('for the sake of'), not a finish; 'in' puts HELD and R inside it. 'by' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck's male is called a sheldrake; the name is often used for the species, a large duck of coasts and estuaries.

clue.text: A rope plaited for show

indicators.note: the strands of the two words are woven together into a new order

explanation.surface: A rope is braided for display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged musical drama, a kind of theatrical production.

clue.text: Composition represented in recital

indicators.note: the word is presented again in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of music performed in a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' is read as re-presented, put together again. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine, a written composition.

clue.text: To help the groom mother invested in dish with hazelnut

parts.note: a curry is a spicy dish

indicators.note: the mother piece is placed inside the nut word, as money is put into something

parts.note: a cob or cobnut is a hazelnut

explanation.surface: A tip for the bridegroom: Mum put money into a nutty dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like a bridegroom but is a stable hand tending horses. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A curry comb is a stiff toothed tool used in a stable for grooming a horse's coat.

clue.text: Storyteller about to complain

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: telling stories means lying, so a storyteller is a liar

explanation.surface: A novelist is about to air a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the turning signal and 'to' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest bitterly or rant against something.

clue.text: Fellow in robbery is a pleasure seeker

indicators.note: the fellow word is placed inside the robbery word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A man taking part in a hold-up is someone after kicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist lives for enjoyment, seeing pleasure as the chief good in life.

clue.text: Move quickly to reverse a wrong

indicators.note: the word is turned round and read from the end

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Act fast to undo an injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait faster than a walk, so to trot is to go at a brisk pace.

clue.text: Sauce bachelor's put in Mexican food

indicators.note: the bachelor piece is placed inside the food word

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican folded tortilla
BA, Bachelor of Arts, plus S for the 's

explanation.surface: A single man's condiment is added to a taco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bachelor' is the degree, BA, not a single man; its 's gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of hot pepper sauce from Louisiana.

clue.text: Met to adopt legal right of striking

indicators.note: the met word takes in the other piece, as a family takes in a child

parts.note: met, as a committee does, means sat
a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: London police take on a legal right to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like London's Metropolitan Police but is the verb, as a court sat. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or most noticeable, as in the salient points.

clue.text: Whereon board stowaway initially had to remove clothing?

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of the word

parts.note: to deck is to dress up, so to undeck is to strip

explanation.surface: On a ship, the stowaway's first act was to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: The print runs 'Where on' together: the definition is a place on board a ship. 'had to' are link words, and the question mark flags the less usual verb 'undeck'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundeck is an open upper deck of a ship where passengers sunbathe.

clue.text: Mounting rubbish brought about trouble in sewer

indicators.note: the turned word is brought around the other piece
in a down clue mounting reads the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A mound of waste caused problems in the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' turns ROT into TOR and 'brought about' puts AIL inside it. 'sewer' is not a drain but one who sews; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sews for a living, making and altering clothes, is a tailor.

clue.text: Good weapon gets the once-over

parts.note: a lance is a long weapon carried by a mounted knight

explanation.surface: A fine weapon is given a quick inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick look, which is what giving something the once-over means.

clue.text: Astronomer lost his head in backstreet

indicators.note: the astronomer's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Edmond Halley was the astronomer who predicted the return of Halley's comet

explanation.surface: A stargazer panicked in a back lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost his head' reads as panicking but removes the H. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow lane behind or between buildings.

clue.text: Prohibition's found everywhere in India

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban; the 's means 'is'
something found everywhere is in abundance, galore

explanation.surface: A ban is in force all over India.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place found 'in India'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now officially Bengaluru, is a large city in southern India.

clue.text: Disagree with rabbi during illness

indicators.note: the rabbi piece comes within the illness word

parts.note: ague is a fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: Quarrel with the rabbi while he is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to quarrel or dispute with someone.

clue.text: Seafood that is great to throw out, in a way

indicators.note: the two pieces are put inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
G is an abbreviation for great
to oust is to throw out

explanation.surface: Seafood that is wonderful to toss away, in a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is', 'to' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is a spiny lobster, eaten as shellfish.

clue.text: Terrible end of term for taletellers

parts.note: grim means terrible or dreadful

indicators.note: takes just the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dreadful finish to the school term for gossips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taletellers' looks like gossips but means storytellers. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected and published German folk tales.

clue.text: Regret game with Spain

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a game
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Sorrow over a match against Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to be sorry for it.

clue.text: Stop landlord appearing in print

parts.note: to stop is to block
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: Prevent the landlord being in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' gives LETTER, one who lets. 'appearing in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Block letters are separate capital letters, the hand forms asked for when told to print.
